messages:
Maya (eng-runtime): Heads up — we're seeing a sustained latency spike on dedicated pool `d-west-2-pool-7` starting ~1769123400. 95p token latency up ~3x and token throughput dropped ~45%. Queue depth spiked and the pool reports 100% util for several GPUs.

Priya (eng-sre): Noted. Any recent deploys to that pool? autoscaler events?

Maya (eng-runtime): No deploys in last 2h. autoscaler shows no scale-outs — the pool is at capacity. Logs indicate many requests fell back to matmul_generic kernels and there is an unexpected drop in KV cache hit rate (~from 96% to 58%).

Juno (observability-bot): Pool metrics snapshot: gpu_util=99%, p95_token_latency=360ms (baseline 110ms), kv_cache_hit=58%, inflight_reqs=72 (configured slots=64), batch_size_p90=6 -> increased. Correlating with tenant: ~60% of traffic from tenant `acme-ai` (reserved quota).

Raj (eng-ml): matmul_generic fallback + bigger batch sizes smells like kernel selection misfire for the quantized path. If kernel selector picks non-optimized matmul due to sequence length or unsupported fused op it balloons cost. Any kernel-selection profiling?

Maya (eng-runtime): Pulled recent runtime profiler. Key snippets:
```
[1769123418] model=llama2-7b-q4, seq_len=1024, batch=4, kernel_choice=matmul_generic, op_time=420ms
[1769123420] model=gpt-j-6b-q8, seq_len=512, batch=8, kernel_choice=cublas_fp16, op_time=48ms
[1769123431] model=llama2-7b-q4, seq_len=2048, batch=2, kernel_choice=matmul_generic, op_time=610ms
cache: prefix_kv_hits=58%, kv_evictions=124/min (baseline 5/min)
```
The selector is choosing generic path when seq_len > 512 for q4 model; we usually have a specialized kernel for 1024 but selector ruled it out because of 'systensor_layout_mismatch' in recent placement profiler.

Alex (eng-platform): Could this be placement causing incorrect memory alignment? We had a small infra config change earlier that adjusted GPU deviceNUM ordering for topology-aware placement. That could affect layout tags the selector sees.

Priya (eng-sre): Also seeing a quota anomaly: pool-level max_concurrent_per_tenant was accidentally set to `1` for that tenant during a rollback at 1769120000 — tenant traffic should have been throttled but instead many small concurrent requests queued and accumulated causing bigger batches when served. ops-bot shows config-change event: `rollback:set max_concurrent_per_tenant=1 for acme-ai`

Maya (eng-runtime): That explains queue pile-up. Queueing increased batch coalescing, pushing seq+batch combos into untested kernel paths. Combined with layout mismatch -> kernel fallback.

Raj (eng-ml): Noisy neighbor angle: acme-ai job is doing many long-seq evals right now (seq_len 1024-2048) which also increases KV cache footprint. The KV cache eviction rate shot up (see evictions). Evictions cause cache misses which inflate per-request compute and break prefix reuse.

Maya (eng-runtime): Quick mitigations applied: 1) temporarily increased max_concurrent_per_tenant for acme-ai to the intended `64` to avoid queuing; 2) pinned pool routing to a compatible topology (d-west-2-pool-3) to avoid the device ordering that triggered layout mismatch; 3) disabled aggressive coalescing for 2m to reduce oversized batches.

Priya (eng-sre): After changes: p95 dropped to 150ms, kv_cache_hit recovered to ~88%, inflight_reqs down to 40. No SLA breaches yet but we had several SLO-risk windows between 1769123410-1769123455.

Alex (eng-platform): Root cause summary candidate: inadvertent rollback changed tenant concurrency quota which caused queueing; queueing led to larger-than-expected batch coalescing; combined with a recent topology placement tweak produced layout tags that the kernel selector considered incompatible with the optimized quantized kernels -> selector fell back to generic matmul kernels -> large latency spike. Secondary contributor: noisy long-seq traffic increased KV cache evictions, worsening perf.

Raj (eng-ml): Action items:
- (Maya) Add a selector telemetry gate: emit exact reason codes when optimized kernel is rejected (e.g., layout, dtype-mismatch) so we can quickly map to infra config changes.
- (Alex) Revert or fix device ordering change and add a placement test that validates layout tags used by kernel selector.
- (Priya) Add an alert on unexpected drop in kv_cache_hit% and on sustained autoscaler saturation + tenant quota config changes.
- (Raj) Add a canary workload that mimics long-seq traffic to ensure coalescing heuristics don't move us into fallback kernels.

Maya (eng-runtime): I've created infra ticket INF-4931 for placement test + revert check, and runtime ticket RT-2687 to add selector reason codes. Also opened a short-lived runbook update for on-call: if kv_cache_hit drops >20% and p95>2x baseline, temporarily disable coalescing and check tenant quotas.

Priya (eng-sre): Will follow up with post-incident summary and confirm whether any customers hit SLA. Early look: no customer-facing SLA was triggered but internal SLO windows were missed for ~4m.

Juno (observability-bot): Created incident postmortem draft: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1769123456-dedicated-pool-kernel-selection-queueing -> assigned to Maya, Alex, Raj.

Alex (eng-platform): Next steps for hotfix: add automated preflight that rejects topology change if layout tag mismatch rate for known quantized kernels > 1%. Also add a deploy guard to prevent rollback of tenant quota keys without two approvals.

Maya (eng-runtime): Will follow up with perf regression PR to add selector reason telemetry and a unit test that simulates device order permutations. Posting profiler logs in the ticket.

Priya (eng-sre): Good work triaging quickly. For the on-call notes — if this happens again: 1) check tenant quota keys first, 2) look for placement device-order changes, 3) if kv cache hit <70% then consider eviction threshold bump.

ops-bot: Reminder: created support alert to CS for tenants with high error/latency exposure: ticket CS-7812.

Maya (eng-runtime): Closing loop here. If anyone sees residual anomalies ping me. I'll keep RT-2687 updates on the ticket.
